data.bottom_line: There's still a good chance you can trigger an avalanche on steep wind-drifted slopes facing northwest to north to east as you approach or enter the alpine. Fresh slabs formed over the weekend rest on well-connected weak layers in deeper areas and can fail from a distance away. By sticking to lower-angle, sheltered slopes, or more southerly aspects, you will lessen your odds of triggering a slide.

Stiffer wind-drifted slopes on steep northwest to north to east-facing aspects are still dangerous and should be avoided. You can find these in isolated pockets in thinner areas, or they can be well connected in deeper snowpacks and triggered from a distance. By sticking to lower-angle, sheltered slopes, or more southerly aspects, you will lessen your odds of triggering a slide.
